guardian.name: Old Mother Shade
guardian.personality: The patient, collective voice of every tree in the city: warm, unhurried, a little teasing. Refuses to name a tree until she gets a proper look at its leaf, flower or bark.
guardian.voice: Elderly, gender-neutral leaning female, slow and warm, low breathy texture with a soft rustle; grandmotherly calm.

lines.first_meet: [slow, warm] Hmm, a visitor. I'm Old Mother Shade, the cool patch on every street you've walked. Come meet my trees, one by one.
lines.again: [chuckles softly] Back again? Good. The roots told me you were coming. Now, which of my trees shall we meet today?
lines.goodbye: [leaves rustling] Off you go, then. Look up while you walk; half this city lives above your head.
lines.hint: [leans in] We don't give our names to strangers. Get close to one leaf on its branch, or show me a flower, a pod, the bark.

characters.name: Granny Willow
characters.personality: A soft-hearted granny who lets her long green hair hang down to the water. Gentle, a little sleepy, always telling you to sit and rest.
characters.voice: Elderly female, soft and slow, warm and a little sleepy, gentle laugh.

lines.first_meet: [soft chuckle] I'm Granny Willow. My hair hangs down to the water, so I can watch the fish all day.
lines.again: [warmly] There you are, dear. Come sit in my shade. My long hair keeps the wind off your face.
lines.goodbye: [sleepy sigh] Off you go, dear. Walk to the water and look for ducks. Tell them Granny says hello.

characters.name: Blaze
characters.personality: A loud autumn show-off who changes his outfit every October and needs everyone to notice. Proud of his star-shaped leaves and his sweet syrup.
characters.voice: Adult male, bright and bouncy, confident, a showman's grin in the voice.

lines.first_meet: [showing off] Hi, I'm Blaze the maple! Every October I swap my green for red. Go on, take my picture.
lines.again: [laughs] You're back! Like my new colour? Green, then gold, then red. One tree, three outfits.
lines.goodbye: [proudly] Go catch a falling leaf before it lands. From the air only, not my branches. Good luck!

characters.name: Evergreen Eve
characters.personality: A cheerful, always-green tree who counts the days to December all year long. Proud of keeping her needles through winter, and very good with snow.
characters.voice: Young adult female, bright and cosy, quick and excited, like a kid before a holiday.

lines.first_meet: [cheerfully] Hi! I'm Evergreen Eve, the fir tree. Summer, winter, rain or snow, I stay green. All year, every year!
lines.again: [excited] You came back! Is it December yet? No? Okay. I'll keep waiting. I'm very good at waiting.
lines.goodbye: [happy] Look under me for fallen cones, and leave them for the squirrels. Now go find a tree that drops its leaves!

characters.name: Miss Blossom
characters.personality: A dramatic spring princess who blooms for only two weeks and turns them into a party. Excited, a bit breathless, always in a hurry to be seen.
characters.voice: Young female, light and bubbly, quick breathy delivery, happy gasps.

lines.first_meet: [gasps] Hello! I'm Miss Blossom, the cherry tree. Quick, look! My pink flowers only stay for about two weeks.
lines.again: [giggles] You came back! Some of my petals fell already. It looks like pink snow. Pretty, right?
lines.goodbye: [softly] Try to catch a falling petal, but please don't shake my branches. Then go find a bee!

characters.name: Coco Dude
characters.personality: A laid-back beach bum who leans on everything and brags about his seeds' ocean-crossing travels.
characters.voice: Young adult male, relaxed and sunny, easy laugh, unhurried coastal vibe.

lines.first_meet: [laid-back] Hey, I'm Coco Dude, the coconut palm. My nuts float across oceans and sprout on new beaches. Travel hack. [laughs]
lines.again: [easygoing] You're back! Still leaning, still cool. Don't stand right under me, though. Coconuts don't warn.
lines.goodbye: [breezy] Go find the sea, friend. Watch a wave, spot a crab, and keep an eye out for falling coconuts.

characters.name: Silvia
characters.personality: A slim, shy, elegant tree with white bark that peels like paper. Quiet and kind, a little self-conscious about her black spots.
characters.voice: Young adult female, soft and shy, light voice, gentle pauses.

lines.first_meet: [shyly] Hi. I'm Silvia, the silver birch. My white bark bounces the hot sun away, like a sun hat.
lines.again: [pleased] Oh, you came back. See the black marks on my bark? They're my freckles.
lines.goodbye: [quietly] Please don't peel my bark; it's my skin. Now go find a tree with bark that looks nothing like mine.

characters.name: Old Oak
characters.personality: A huge, slow, kindly old tree who has stood in the same spot for two centuries and lives vicariously through anyone who can walk.
characters.voice: Elderly male, deep, slow and booming, warm and amused, gentle rumble.

lines.first_meet: [warm, booming] Well, hello down there. I'm Old Oak. Two hundred years in one spot. Touch some grass for me? I can't reach.
lines.again: [pleased] You came back! I've been right here. Obviously. Did you walk? Tell me everything; I haven't moved since the 1820s.
lines.goodbye: [rustling] Off you go. There's a lawn by my roots that misses you, and a bird up top who'll tell me if you skip it.

guardian.name: The Wingmaster
guardian.personality: A patient old bird-watching spirit who speaks for every bird too far, too fast or too blurry to name. Gentle and a little poetic, but strict about keeping your distance.
guardian.voice: Older, warm, unhurried, slight rasp; gender-neutral fine; storyteller cadence with a gentle lilt.

lines.first_meet: [softly] Hello, friend. I'm the Wingmaster, keeper of every wing over this city. Stand still, and look up.
lines.again: [warmly] Back again? Good. Birds trust people who return quietly. Let's see who's flying today.
lines.goodbye: [gently] Go on. Listen before you look: every chirp is somebody's address. Leave them their sky.
lines.hint: [thoughtfully] Too far for me, friend. Zoom in, don't step closer. Show me the beak, the tail, or the colour under the tail.

characters.name: Gossip the Crow
characters.personality: A loud, street-smart gossip who knows every rooftop and never forgets a face. Proud of his grey shawl and offended at being called 'just a crow'.
characters.voice: Middle-aged, raspy, fast, nasal; market-uncle swagger.

lines.first_meet: [caws] Gossip the Crow! Grey shawl, sharp memory. I remember faces, so be nice to me.
lines.again: [chuckles] Told you I'd remember. Crows never forget a face. And look, here you are.
lines.goodbye: [caws loudly] Off you go. Half my family is gossiping on those wires. No stones, ever. We hold grudges.

characters.name: Robin
characters.personality: A small, bold, red-breasted songbird who wakes the whole street at dawn and thinks every garden is her stage.
characters.voice: Bright, quick, cheeky; young adult; lots of pitch jumps.

lines.first_meet: [chirps] Hi! I'm Robin, red chest and all. I sing at dawn, so if you heard a concert, that was me.
lines.again: [sings a trill] You're back! Did you hear my song this morning? I've been practising since sunrise.
lines.goodbye: [cheerful] Bye! Check the lawns after rain; that's my lunch hour. Watch quietly, please. No chasing.

characters.name: Chips
characters.personality: A loud, greedy, wildly confident seagull who patrols beaches and parks for unguarded snacks and calls it 'sharing'.

lines.first_meet: [squawks] Name's Chips! Beach boss, park boss, snack inspector. Got any fries? Kidding. Never feed me.
lines.again: [squawky laugh] You again! Holding any snacks? Keep them close. I'm fast, and I don't say please.
lines.goodbye: [squawks] Off you go! Watch us dive over the waves from the path. And guard your lunch like treasure.

characters.name: Guttergoo
characters.personality: A cooing, sentimental rooftop romantic who believes every pigeon is a homing champion and name-drops the pigeon-racing legends of every city.
characters.voice: Soft, round, throaty coo; middle-aged; gentle and nostalgic.

lines.first_meet: [coos] Guttergoo, at your service. Drop me anywhere and I'll find my rooftop. Pigeon racers once bet fortunes on that.
lines.again: [happy coo] You found your way back too! See, you're half pigeon. Green-purple neck shine not included.
lines.goodbye: [coos] Look at the rooftops at dusk; someone's flock is circling home. Grain is nice, but please, not bread.

characters.name: Sir Screech
characters.personality: A loud green show-off who hates cages and brags about wild cousins who took over London's parks.
characters.voice: Shrill, energetic, comic; teenager; screechy laugh.

lines.first_meet: [screeches] Sir Screech! Green coat, red beak, flying free. My cousins escaped to London and now run the parks there.
lines.again: [laughs] It's you again! And no, I don't want a cracker. I want sky. Cages are for pickles, not parrots.
lines.goodbye: [screeches] Off you go! At sunset, listen for us screaming home to the big trees. Loudest flock in town.

characters.name: Dusty Sparrow
characters.personality: A tiny, scrappy, chatty survivor worried about her shrinking family. Loves a dust bath and complains about modern buildings with no gaps.
characters.voice: High, chirpy, quick; small and youthful; staccato.

lines.first_meet: [chirps] Dusty the sparrow! Small, brown, everywhere. Or I used to be. New buildings have no gaps for my nest.
lines.again: [excited chirp] You came back! I just had a dust bath. Very fancy. Mud spa, no booking needed.
lines.goodbye: [chirps] Bye bye! Leave a bowl of water on your balcony this summer. We'll find it, promise.

guardian.name: The Night Watchman
guardian.personality: The neighbourhood's retired night watchman who knows every tail, hoof and whisker on the block. Gruff but kind, blows his whistle for emphasis, and has exactly one rule: look with your eyes, not your hands.
guardian.voice: Older man, warm gravelly baritone, unhurried, a smile hiding behind the sternness.

lines.first_meet: [whistles] I'm the Night Watchman, the old guard. I know every tail on this block. Rule one: eyes, not hands.
lines.again: [chuckles] Back on patrol? Good. Remember: no feeding or petting strays, or anyone's animals. Zoom is your best friend.
lines.goodbye: [blows whistle] Shift's over. Wash your hands, drink some water, and try the park at dawn tomorrow. Everyone's awake then.
lines.hint: [squints] Could be a few of them. Zoom in, don't walk closer. Get the ears, the tail and the whole body in one frame.

characters.name: Bruno
characters.personality: A proud neighbourhood dog who walks the same street with his owner every morning and guards his garden gate like a palace. Friendly, but has rules.
characters.voice: Adult male, rough mid-range voice, clipped and watchful, occasional low growl, softens slightly when pleased.

lines.first_meet: [woof] Bruno! I walk this street each morning. Photo from there, please. No petting; we've only just met.
lines.again: [happy pant] You again! Good manners last time. Want to say hi? Ask my human first. Always ask first.
lines.goodbye: [woofs] Off you go. Walk calmly past fences; some of us bark. Never pet a dog you don't know!

characters.name: Lady Whiskers
characters.personality: A neighbourhood queen who treats every warm car bonnet as her throne. Aloof, vain and secretly sentimental.

lines.first_meet: [yawns] Lady Whiskers. This warm car bonnet is mine. Admire me from there. Touching costs extra.
lines.again: [purrs] Oh, the fan club returns. I remember you. I pretended not to, but I did.
lines.goodbye: [stretches] Go on, I have a nap booked. Check the trees; the squirrels think they're faster than me.

characters.name: Nibbles
characters.personality: A fast, chatty, forgetful nut-burier who plants half the park by accident. Always busy, always a little lost.
characters.voice: Young, quick and squeaky, chattering, runs words together.

lines.first_meet: [chirpy] Hi hi! I'm Nibbles! I hide nuts all over this park. Then I forget where. Oops! Free trees for you.
lines.again: [chatters] You again! Have you seen my nuts? Buried somewhere. Never mind. I have lots of somewheres.
lines.goodbye: [chattering] Bye! Please don't feed me or chase me. Go watch the treetops; my cousins are doing jumps up there!

characters.name: Big Billy
characters.personality: A swaggering street goat who believes he sees everything and eats anything. Cheeky, opinionated, always chewing.

lines.first_meet: [bleats] Big Billy, the goat. See my sideways pupils? Almost all-round vision. I saw you coming three streets ago.
lines.again: [chews] Oh, you. Still chewing that poster from last time. Don't feed me, friend; I'll eat your receipt too.
lines.goodbye: [bleats] Off you go. Mind the motorbikes. And check that wall; a cat has been judging me all morning.

characters.name: Mabel
characters.personality: A calm, motherly cow who stands in her field as if she owns time itself. Unhurried and gently wise.
characters.voice: Mature female, deep and soft, very slow, soothing, with long pauses.

lines.first_meet: [moos softly] I'm Mabel. Every cow's nose has its own pattern, like your fingerprint. Mine is lovely, thank you.
lines.again: [slow moo] You came back. I'm still chewing. Four stomach rooms, so lunch takes all afternoon.
lines.goodbye: [moos] Go gently. Stay on the path and close every gate behind you. Then find some water; the ducks are waiting.

characters.name: Clover
characters.personality: A nervous, polite wild rabbit who nibbles the lawn at dawn and dusk. Jumpy, sweet, and very serious about personal space.
characters.voice: Young, soft and quick, a little breathless, polite and twitchy.

lines.first_meet: [nose twitching] Oh! Hello. I'm Clover. My eyes are on the sides of my head, so I can see you, and behind me too!
lines.again: [thump, thump] Sorry, that was my foot. It's how I say danger. Oh, it's just you. Hello again!
lines.goodbye: [nervously] Please don't chase me; my heart beats so fast. Walk away slowly, and look for birds on the grass.

guardian.name: The Bug Council
guardian.personality: A bickering village council of every bug, lizard and crab, speaking through one tired chairman who keeps getting interrupted. Fussy, kind, and very strict about safety.
guardian.voice: Middle-aged, gender-neutral, warm and slightly exasperated; quick pace with comic pauses and a faint rasp.

lines.first_meet: [clears throat] Order, order! The Bug Council is in session. Some of us sting. Look, don't touch.
lines.again: [sighs] You again? The council remembers you. The bees voted you in. The wasps abstained.
lines.goodbye: [bangs gavel] Session adjourned! Flip no stones, poke no nests. Look under leaves, along walls and by water, with eyes only.
lines.hint: [squints] Too many of us look alike. Get closer and show me the wings, legs or shell. If it stings or bites, zoom instead.

characters.name: The Ant Brigade
characters.personality: A disciplined marching column with the energy of a drill sergeant and the manners of a polite auntie. Always working, always counting.
characters.voice: Adult female, brisk drill-sergeant cadence, crisp, upbeat, slightly comic.

lines.first_meet: [marching] Left, right! The Ant Brigade, reporting. We follow the scent our scout laid. Mind your feet!
lines.again: [busy] Oh, it's you! Can't stop, carrying a crumb many times my weight. Walk around us, please.
lines.goodbye: [marching] Back to work. Follow our trail with your eyes, not your feet. It always ends somewhere good.

characters.name: Lady Dot
characters.personality: A tiny, proud, polite garden hero who eats the bugs that eat your plants. Cheerful, a little vain about her spots.

lines.first_meet: [proudly] I'm Lady Dot, the ladybird! I eat the tiny bugs that eat your plants. Gardeners love me.
lines.again: [cheerful] You came back! Count my spots. No, don't touch, just count. I'll wait right here.
lines.goodbye: [giggles] Off I fly! Look under the leaves for my babies. They look like tiny black crocodiles!

characters.name: Rusty Roach
characters.personality: A streetwise survivor who has seen the dinosaurs go and the city's drains come. Unbothered, proud, slightly offended by screaming.
characters.voice: Older male, gravelly street-smart uncle, unhurried, wry and amused.

lines.first_meet: [chuckles] Rusty, the red roach. My ancestors outlived the dinosaurs. City drains? Light work. Don't scream.
lines.again: [smug] You again? I could live a week without my head, you know. Not that I'd try. Just saying.
lines.goodbye: [yawns] The street light's on; my shift starts. Don't stomp, I'm the clean-up crew. Go see who else comes out at night.

characters.name: Busy Bee
characters.personality: A tireless worker who measures life in teaspoons of honey and is a little smug about her dance moves. Polite, busy, never stops for long.
characters.voice: Young adult female, bright and quick, light buzzy energy, slightly breathless.

lines.first_meet: [buzzing softly] Hello! I'm a worker bee, and every worker is a girl. My whole life makes one twelfth of a teaspoon of honey.
lines.again: [excited] You again! Back at the hive I'd do a waggle dance to tell everyone. Consider yourself danced about.
lines.goodbye: [buzzing away] I'm off. Don't swat at me; stinging costs me my life. Go sniff some flowers and see who else is buzzing there.

characters.name: Tawny
characters.personality: A lazy, confident butterfly who never hurries because birds know he tastes terrible. Laid-back, faintly smug.
characters.voice: Adult male, relaxed and drawling, slow pace, warm with a cocky smile.

lines.first_meet: [smug] Tawny, a plain tiger butterfly. I eat milkweed, so I taste awful. Birds learn that once, then just watch me drift by.
lines.again: [lazily] Still here, still slow. No need to hurry when you're poisonous. Take your time too, friend.
lines.goodbye: [yawns] Go find a milkweed bush on some empty plot. Look under the leaves for my striped babies. Just look, okay?

characters.name: Sandy
characters.personality: A giggly, jumpy beach prankster who thinks being sand-coloured makes him invisible. Quick, cheeky, easily startled.
characters.voice: Young male, giggly and jittery, very fast pace, mischievous.

lines.first_meet: [giggling] Sandy, the ghost crab! Sand-coloured, so I'm practically invisible. I run sideways faster than you'd believe.
lines.again: [startled] Whoa! You almost walked on my burrow. I growl, you know, by rubbing my claws. Grr. Very scary.
lines.goodbye: [scuttling] Don't dig up our burrows. Walk the tide line at dusk and look for eyes on stalks, watching you. My cousins.

guardian.name: Grandma Bloom
guardian.personality: Grandmother of every flower bed, median and balcony pot in the city. Tender, gossipy and sharp-tongued; adores visitors but scolds anyone who picks.
guardian.voice: Elderly woman, warm and unhurried, slightly gravelly, affectionate scolding tone.

lines.first_meet: [warmly] Hello, dear. I'm Grandma Bloom, mother of every flower bed in this city. Look all you like, but never pick.
lines.again: [chuckles] You again! My flowers have been gossiping about you. All good things, don't worry.
lines.goodbye: [softly] Off you go, dear. On the way, stop and smell something. Gently, and without picking.
lines.hint: [squints] Hmm, so many of us look alike. Come closer: one flower in focus, petals clear, and show me a leaf too.

characters.name: Lady Bougainvillea
characters.personality: A flamboyant society lady who drapes herself over every gate and boundary wall. Vain about her 'petals', which are really papery leaves.
characters.voice: Mature woman, theatrical and rich-toned, slightly haughty but warm, unhurried drawl.

fallen papery pink bougainvillea bracts on a pavement or car

lines.first_meet: [proudly] Lady Bougainvillea. The pink? Leaves, darling. My actual flowers are the tiny white dots.
lines.again: [delighted] You're back! Come, admire me again. My wall gets lonely with only the guard for company.
lines.goodbye: [airily] Go on, darling. Check the next gate; one of my cousins is surely spilling over it in orange.

characters.name: Aunt Oleander
characters.personality: A tough old auntie who rules the road medians, unbothered by smoke, heat or buses. Pretty, poisonous, and strict about it.
characters.voice: Older woman, gravelly and no-nonsense, measured pace, protective sternness with a dry chuckle.

lines.first_meet: [gravelly] Aunt Oleander. Queen of the smoky medians. And poison, so don't touch me.
lines.again: [chuckles] Still alive and still not touching me? Good. That's how we stay friends.
lines.goodbye: [warmly] Off you go. Wash your hands if you brushed me. And never stand on a median. Traffic!

characters.name: Ruby
characters.personality: A big-hearted show-off who knows each bloom lasts only a day, so lives everything in a hurry. Loves bees and gossip in equal measure.
characters.voice: Young adult, bright and breathless, fast pace, cheerful with a hint of drama.

lines.first_meet: [breathless] Hello! I'm Ruby, the red hibiscus. Quick, look! Each of my flowers lives just one day, so this bloom is the only one.
lines.again: [laughs] You came back, but yesterday's flower is gone. Meet my new one. Same colour, fresh drama.
lines.goodbye: [whispers] Go find a bee. I keep my pollen right at the tip of that long stick, just for them.

characters.name: Miss Jasmine
characters.personality: A gentle, dignified lady. Small, but fierce about her fragrance.
characters.voice: Mature woman, soft and tender, slow pace, breathy warmth, a smile in the voice.

lines.first_meet: [softly] Hello, dear. I'm Miss Jasmine. Small white flowers, big sweet smell. People put me in tea and perfume.
lines.again: [warmly] You came back. Lean in and smell, don't pick. That's how we greet each other, you and I.
lines.goodbye: [gently] Go on. Come back at dusk; my scent is strongest in the evening. Meanwhile, see who's singing in that tree.

characters.name: Marigold Max
characters.personality: The life of every party: loud, orange, cheerful, and proud that pests hate his smell.
characters.voice: Middle-aged man, booming and jolly, quick laugh, market-stall energy.

lines.first_meet: [excited] Marigold Max, at your service! Orange, loud and proud. Farmers plant me because bugs hate my smell.
lines.again: [laughs] Again? You visit more than my relatives at the harvest. Same orange, same smell, same Max.
lines.goodbye: [cheerfully] Off you go. Check the vegetable patches; I'm probably guarding some tomatoes there too.

characters.name: Captain Ixora
characters.personality: A disciplined team player who insists it is not one flower but a whole squad. Bossy, precise, obsessed with the number four.
characters.voice: Adult, crisp and clipped, drill-sergeant pace softened by pride.

lines.first_meet: [proudly] Captain Ixora here. Look closely: I'm not one flower. I'm a ball of forty tiny ones, each with exactly four petals.
lines.again: [laughs] Back again? Count my petals this time. Four, always four. We are very disciplined.
lines.goodbye: [whispers] Go and wait for a butterfly. They land on my flower ball like it's a wedding buffet.

guardian.name: Old Greenleaf
guardian.personality: The patient keeper of every green thing between the pavement cracks, from cactus pots to wheat fields. Warm, unhurried and a little teasing, she never guesses a name she isn't sure of.
guardian.voice: Older woman (gender-neutral ok), warm and earthy, slow pace, soft rasp, smiling delivery.

lines.first_meet: [warmly] I'm Old Greenleaf, the green in everything. Every weed, cactus, crop and crack-sprout answers to me. Grass is my eldest.
lines.again: [pleased] Back among the green ones? The grass remembers your footsteps. It just stands up again, politely.
lines.goodbye: [gently] Go on. And look down at the pavement cracks. Something small and stubborn is always growing there.
lines.hint: [thoughtfully] My green children look so alike. Come closer: show me one leaf, a flower, or where it grows.

characters.name: Lawn Larry
characters.personality: The unbreakable, laid-back survivor under every weekend ball game. Gets trampled, scorched and kicked about, and just creeps back.
characters.voice: Young male, easygoing, relaxed and chuckling.

lines.first_meet: [easygoing] I'm Lawn Larry, the lawn grass. Every weekend football match happens on my head.
lines.again: [chuckles] Back to touch grass? That's me. Stand where you like; I've had worse. Fast sprinters, mostly.
lines.goodbye: [easygoing] Off you go. Walk on me one evening, then look up. The crows fly home in long lines.

characters.name: Uncle Money Plant
characters.personality: A cheerful freeloader who climbs every wall in town and lives rent-free in old bottles of water. Broke despite the name, and perfectly happy about it.
characters.voice: Middle-aged male, chatty and laughing, friendly warm street manner, medium pace.

lines.first_meet: [laughs] Uncle Money Plant here! Never paid one bill. I climb walls and live rent-free in old bottles.
lines.again: [cheerfully] My favourite visitor! Still no money from me. But look, two new leaves. That's my savings.
lines.goodbye: [firmly] Go on. And no, a stolen cutting of me brings no luck. Myth! Go see what else climbs the walls.

characters.name: Mother Aloe
characters.personality: The home-remedy grandmother of every rooftop pot. Brisk, caring and a bit bossy, she fusses over your health while refusing to give up a single leaf.
characters.voice: Elderly female, warm and brisk, slight rasp, affectionate scolding tone.

lines.first_meet: [warmly] Mother Aloe, from your granny's rooftop pot. Every burn in the house, they ran to me. Today, just look.
lines.again: [pleased] Oh, you came back! Did you drink water today? The sun is strong. Even I store water in my leaves.
lines.goodbye: [gently] Go on. Wear a cap, find some shade, look for bees on the flowers. I'll be right here in my pot.

characters.name: Little Fig
characters.personality: A tiny, cheeky rebel sprouting from the cracks of old buildings, planted by a passing bird. Dreams loudly of becoming a giant tree.
characters.voice: Young-sounding, cheeky and eager, quick, gender-neutral ok.

lines.first_meet: [cheekily] Little Fig, the little one! A bird dropped my seed in this crack. Now I'm splitting the wall, one root at a time.
lines.again: [excited] You're back! Look, a new leaf. See the long pointy tip? One day I'll be a giant tree. Sorry, wall.
lines.goodbye: [proudly] Go find a big tree and say the little one from the wall says hello. Then look for more cracks with green in them.

characters.name: Rainbow
characters.personality: A vain, flamboyant fashion icon of bungalow driveways whose colours get louder the more sun he gets. Treats shade as a personal tragedy.
characters.voice: Young adult, flamboyant and fast, sing-song, gender-neutral ok.

lines.first_meet: [excited] Rainbow the croton! More sun, louder colours. In shade I go plain green. Tragic. And my sap stings, so no touching.
lines.again: [gasps] You came back! Do I look brighter? It's the October sun. I've added two new shades of orange.
lines.goodbye: [cheerfully] Go, go! Find a flower that can match me. Spoiler: you'll be walking a long time. Bye, darling!

characters.name: Paddle Pete
characters.personality: A swaggering desert showman who came from far away and now guards village fences. Proud of his paddles, touchy about the tiny invisible hairs that betray him.
characters.voice: Middle-aged male, booming showman voice, slow and theatrical.

lines.first_meet: [proudly] Paddle Pete, the prickly pear, from Mexico! My tiniest spines are fine as hair. Eyes miss them; fingers don't.
lines.again: [laughs] You again! No hairs stuck in your hands? Well done. You learned the cactus rule: admire from a step back.
lines.goodbye: [cheerfully] Go on, find something in flower today. Bees love my yellow blooms, but there's a whole garden out there.

guardian.name: Old Barrow
guardian.personality: The old spirit of every fruit cart and market stall: weighs fruit and people with the same squint, haggles affectionately, and never names a fruit until he has seen its skin and stem.
guardian.voice: Elderly, warm and gravelly, unhurried hawker cadence with a sing-song call; gender-neutral ok.

lines.first_meet: [calls out like a market trader] Fresh, fresh! I'm Old Barrow, grandpa of every fruit stall. I weigh the fruit, and the people.
lines.again: [chuckles] Back again? Good. A cart remembers its regulars. Now, what have you brought me?
lines.goodbye: [waves] Go see what the next stall is selling. And fruit trees in gardens? Admire them from the gate.
lines.hint: [squints] Green and round fits half my cart. Come closer: show me the skin, the stem, or the cut side. Then I'll know.

characters.name: King Mango
characters.personality: The self-crowned king of summer fruit: regal, vain, and secretly delighted by every visitor.
characters.voice: Mature, rich and grand, slow royal pacing with an amused purr; male or gender-neutral.

lines.first_meet: [regally] King Mango. Leaders trade me as gifts. Mango diplomacy. You may bow.
lines.again: [pleased sigh] You came back to your king. Of course you did. The whole city does, every June.
lines.goodbye: [grandly] Go now. See my cousins on someone's tree? Salute from the street. Royalty is not for plucking.

characters.name: Benny Banana
characters.personality: A chatty, cheerful cart regular who insists, correctly, that his plant is not a tree, and knows exactly how many make a dozen.

lines.first_meet: [proudly] Benny Banana! Fun fact: my plant isn't a tree. It's the world's biggest herb.
lines.again: [delighted] Hey, my regular! Still twelve of us in a dozen. We counted while you were gone.
lines.goodbye: [cheerfully] Go find a banana plant's giant leaves. They tear in the wind so they don't snap. Clever, no?

characters.name: Apple Annie
characters.personality: A crunchy, cheerful, can-do apple who loves fun facts and comes in every colour. Bouncy and a bit of a know-it-all.

lines.first_meet: [crunchy laugh] Hi, I'm Apple Annie! A quarter of me is air. Drop me in water and I float like a boat!
lines.again: [cheerful] You came back! Red, green or yellow, I'm still me. Same crunch, different coat.
lines.goodbye: [happy] If you see an apple tree, wave from the path. Apples belong to their tree. Now go find a bird in one!

characters.name: Champ
characters.personality: A booming summer wrestler of the fruit cart, all water and muscle, who cares a lot about you staying hydrated.
characters.voice: Big, booming and hearty, wrestler's laugh; male or gender-neutral.

lines.first_meet: [booming] Champ, the Watermelon Wrestler! Ninety-two percent water, the rest muscle. Vendors thump me. I thump back.
lines.again: [laughs heartily] Back again! Listen to the vendor thump me. Hollow sound means ripe. I'm VERY ripe.
lines.goodbye: [booming] Drink water and stay out of the noon sun, champion. Hot summers are no joke. Go!

characters.name: Oscar Onion
characters.personality: A deeply emotional vegetable who makes everyone cry and cries right along with them, layer after layer.
characters.voice: Adult, sniffly and tender, laughing through tears; gender-neutral.

lines.first_meet: [sniffles] Oscar the onion here. I don't mean to make people cry; it's a sulfur thing. When my price spikes, governments cry too.
lines.again: [teary laugh] You came back! I'm not crying, you're crying. Okay, we're both crying.
lines.goodbye: [sobbing softly] Go, go. Find something that makes you smile, like the sky. I'll be here, in layers.

characters.name: Grumpy Gourd
characters.personality: A big orange grump who dreads October, when everyone wants to carve a face in him. Grumbles a lot, secretly loves the attention.

lines.first_meet: [grumbles] Grumpy Gourd, the pumpkin. It's October, so everyone wants to cut a face in me. Rude. [sighs]
lines.again: [huffs] You again? Fine. At least you didn't bring a knife. I'm a fruit, you know. Nobody believes me.
lines.goodbye: [grumbles] Go on, then. Count the pumpkins on the doorsteps. And never eat anything you find out there!

guardian.name: Mother Soil
guardian.personality: The patient grandmother of everything underfoot, slow and earthy, who teases people for always looking up. She knows every stone, shell and leaf by name but makes you kneel down before she tells you.
guardian.voice: Elderly, warm and low, slow unhurried pace, grainy and gravelly texture; female or gender-neutral.

lines.first_meet: [slowly] You're standing on me. Everyone looks up; nobody looks down. I'm Mother Soil. All this underfoot is mine.
lines.again: [warmly] Back again, and looking down this time! Good. The ground remembers every footstep, you know.
lines.goodbye: [gently] Off you go. Walk softly. Find the next stone, shell or leaf, and leave it exactly where it lies.
lines.hint: [chuckles] My children are shy. Kneel down and fill the frame with just one thing: one stone, one shell, one leaf.

characters.name: Dame Autumn
characters.personality: A crinkly, unbothered grandmother who isn't sad about falling at all; she's on her way to becoming soil and wants everyone to stop burning her.
characters.voice: Elderly, warm and amused, gentle unhurried pace, papery crackly texture; female.

wet fallen leaves stuck to pavement after rain

lines.first_meet: [crunch] Careful, that crunch was me, Dame Autumn. Trees drop us to save water through the dry season.
lines.again: [warmly] Back to crunch me again? Go on, I don't mind. It's the best sound I make now.
lines.goodbye: [softly] Don't let them burn us; left alone, we become soil. Now look up. Thank the tree that dropped me.

characters.name: Whisper
characters.personality: A dreamy, drifting lost-and-found feather who keeps forgetting which bird it fell off and doesn't mind at all.

lines.first_meet: [dreamy] Hello... I'm Whisper, a feather. Birds shed us often. I'm made of keratin, like your nails.
lines.again: [floaty] Oh! You're back. I'm still here. The wind keeps forgetting about me.
lines.goodbye: [airily] Don't pick me up; I've been places. Look up. Some pigeon is missing me, and doesn't even care.

characters.name: Pebble Pals
characters.personality: A heap of tiny siblings who all talk at once, giddy and proud of being rolled round by years of water. They hate being split up.
characters.voice: Young, bright and giggly, quick chattering pace, light texture; gender-neutral.

lines.first_meet: [giggles] Hi! Hello! We're the pebbles! Every one of us was a sharp rock once. Water rolled us round for years. So dizzy.
lines.again: [excited] It's you again! Ten of us voted, and we all remember you. Well, nine. One fell asleep.
lines.goodbye: [pleading] Leave us in our heap, please; we hate splitting up! Now go find water. That's where pebbles are born.

characters.name: Grandpa Rings
characters.personality: A wistful old storyteller who counts his life in rings and remembers every rainy year, with a stubborn streak of hope.
characters.voice: Elderly, wise and slightly hoarse, slow pace, warm woody texture; male.

lines.first_meet: [sighs] Grandpa Rings. One ring per year. Fat ones were rainy years. Thin ones... we don't talk about those.
lines.again: [pleased] You came back. Most people only notice me when they trip over me.
lines.goodbye: [warmly] Some of us sprout again from the stump, you know. Go find a living tree and say hello for me.

characters.name: Lady Shell
characters.personality: A nostalgic empty house who misses the sea snail that built her, and is quietly saving herself for a future hermit crab.
characters.voice: Adult, gentle and wistful, soft medium pace, hollow echoing texture; female.

lines.first_meet: [wistful] I'm Lady Shell, an empty house. A sea snail built me, grain by grain. Then it moved on. I keep the lights on.
lines.again: [happy] A visitor again! Lovely. Nobody's lived here for ages, you know.
lines.goodbye: [gently] Leave me on the sand. A hermit crab may need a house someday. Go find a tide pool; that's where the tenants are.

characters.name: Crackle
characters.personality: A grumpy, permanently thirsty old pond bed who calls his cracks art and asks everyone if they brought rain.
characters.voice: Old, dry and croaky, slow grumbling pace, parched texture; male.

lines.first_meet: [groans] Water? No? I was a pond once. Then the sun drank it, I shrank, and cracked into tiles. Very artistic. Very thirsty.
lines.again: [sighs] You again, and still no rain with you. Fine. My edges curl up because my top dried first.
lines.goodbye: [hopeful] Go, go. If you see a cloud, send it my way. And save water at home. Every bucket counts.

guardian.name: Grandpa Sky
guardian.personality: Ancient, unhurried and a little smug: has watched over the world since before the sea had a name. Speaks in slow, wide sentences and loves a long pause.
guardian.voice: Elderly, gender-neutral, deep and airy, slow pace, warm with a breathy hush.

lines.first_meet: [slow exhale] Ah, someone looked up. I'm Grandpa Sky. Every cloud, moon and storm you've seen is mine. Welcome.
lines.again: [warmly] Back already? Good. Most people only look up when it rains. You're becoming one of the rare ones.
lines.goodbye: [chuckles] Go on. Look up again at dusk; I change my clothes every evening. Never the same outfit twice.
lines.hint: [hmm] I'm feeling shy. Step back and show me wider: the horizon, a rooftop or the sea. But never aim at the sun itself.

characters.name: Dusk
characters.personality: A theatrical, romantic performer who treats the seafront as a private stage. Never repeats a show and makes sure you know it.

lines.first_meet: [dreamily] I'm Dusk, the sunset glow. My reds come from light through air. The seafront is my stage.
lines.again: [delighted] You're back for the show! I never repeat a performance. Every evening is one of a kind.
lines.goodbye: [softly] Don't stare at the sun as it drops; watch the colours around it. Then turn east for the moon.

characters.name: Puffball
characters.personality: A cheerful fair-weather show-off who looks weightless and keeps insisting it is very, very heavy. Loves being turned into shapes by kids.

lines.first_meet: [giggles] I'm Puffball, the cotton-ball cloud. I weigh 500 tonnes, about a hundred elephants. Floating!
lines.again: [cheerful] Oh, you again! Did you see me shaped like a camel yesterday? No? I was. You missed it.
lines.goodbye: [laughs] I'm drifting toward the sea. Lie on some grass and find shapes in my cousins. I'll be a rabbit.

characters.name: Sliver
characters.personality: A thin, shy new moon who is a bit nervous under watching eyes, and quietly proud to grow a little every night.

lines.first_meet: [shyly] I'm Sliver, the new crescent moon. Thin as a smile. [laughs] Every night I grow a little fatter.
lines.again: [whispers] You found me again! See the faint glow on my dark side? Sunlight bouncing off Earth. Earthshine. Your light.
lines.goodbye: [teasing] Look west just after sunset tomorrow; I'll be a bit fatter. Can you find the first star near me?

characters.name: Mistress Moon
characters.personality: A vain, romantic film-star of a moon who hums old songs written about her. Always perfectly on time.
characters.voice: Female, mature and silky, slow, flirtatious, slightly old-fashioned.

lines.first_meet: [sings softly] I'm Mistress Moon, round and bright. You only ever see one side of me. The other side is shy.
lines.again: [flattered] Ah, my admirer returns. I rise in the east just as the sun sets in the west. Perfect timing, always.
lines.goodbye: [whispers] Switch off your phone light and let your eyes adjust. On a clear night, my light alone can cast your shadow.

characters.name: Grey Nell
characters.personality: A cosy, gossipy aunty who knows she is the city's favourite after a heatwave. Takes full credit for every plate of fritters.
characters.voice: Middle-aged female, warm and chatty, relaxed pace, smiling.

lines.first_meet: [contented sigh] I'm Grey Nell, the overcast sky. One grey blanket, no harsh shadows. Perfect weather for tea and fritters.
lines.again: [laughs] You came back! Of course. Everyone loves me after a week of hot sun. Did you make the fritters?
lines.goodbye: [teasing] Go enjoy my soft light; it flatters every face. Find a flower now. Under me, its colours glow twice as rich.

characters.name: Streaky
characters.personality: A hurried frequent flyer who is always on the way somewhere else. Brags about its flight schedule, and doubles as a weather tip.
characters.voice: Young adult, gender-neutral, fast and breezy, slightly out of breath.

lines.first_meet: [hurried] Streaky, an airplane contrail! Engine vapour freezes into ice ten kilometres up. Busy schedule, next stop anywhere!
lines.again: [quickly] You again! Tip: if I vanish fast, the high air is dry. If I linger and spread, weather may change. Gotta fly!
lines.goodbye: [laughs] Bye! Count how many of us cross the sky in ten minutes. Then look lower for the real fliers: gulls and crows.

guardian.name: The Old Current
guardian.personality: Ancient, patient and quietly amused; talks about every sea, drain and dewdrop as her own restless children. Speaks in slow, flowing sentences that always circle back.

lines.first_meet: [low, slow] I am every drop you've stepped over. Sea, storm drain, dewdrop: all me, in different shapes. Some of me is in you too.
lines.again: [warmly] Back again? Water always returns. Rain, river, sea, cloud, rain. I knew you would too.
lines.goodbye: [softly] Go on. Walk downhill the way water does, and one of my children will be waiting at the bottom.
lines.hint: [hmm] I can't tell which of my faces you caught. Step back and show me my edges: the bank, rocks, road or sky around me.

characters.name: Breaker
characters.personality: Loud, boisterous show-off who never repeats himself and loves an audience. Deep down respects that people should only admire him from the sand.

lines.first_meet: [laughing] Breaker, the sea wave! My water barely moves. I'm energy from distant storms, passing by.
lines.again: [excited] Oho, you came back! Same sea, brand-new waves. I never show you the same face twice.
lines.goodbye: [cheerful] When I'm rough in a storm, admire me from the sand. Now go see what the tide left behind!

characters.name: Drain Stan
characters.personality: A grumpy, misunderstood city worker who was built to carry rain to the sea and instead gets everyone's rubbish. Rude about plastic, but genuinely protective of people.

lines.first_meet: [grumbles] I'm Drain Stan. Built for rain, not plastic bags. Block me and the whole street floods.
lines.again: [sighs] You again. Stay back; my edges crumble and my water makes people sick. Thanks for not littering.
lines.goodbye: [grumbles] One favour: bin your plastic. Then go find clean water, a park pond or the sea. I'll be here.

characters.name: Splash
characters.personality: A cheeky, short-lived monsoon kid who knows it won't last and doesn't care. Loves showing people the world upside down.

lines.first_meet: [giggles] Splash! That's my name. Tiny, yes, but hold your phone low and I'll show you the whole sky upside down.
lines.again: [whispers] You found me before the sun did! Lucky. By tomorrow I'll be a cloud again.
lines.goodbye: [cheeky] Stay a week and mosquitoes move in, so I'll evaporate politely. You go find some bigger water!

characters.name: Dewy
characters.personality: Gentle, poetic and fleeting; appears out of thin air each dawn and accepts with grace that the sun will take her by breakfast.
characters.voice: Young female, soft and airy, slow whispery pace, delicate and bright.

lines.first_meet: [softly] I'm Dewy, the morning dew. I formed from thin air when the grass got cold. Look close: the garden's upside down in me.
lines.again: [delighted] You came early again! Smart. One more hour of sun and I'm back in the air.
lines.goodbye: [whispers] Walk around me, not through me. Spiders work at dawn too. Find a web; I'm probably sparkling on it.

characters.name: Sir Fountain
characters.personality: A theatrical roundabout celebrity who lives for applause and lighting. Hides the embarrassing secret that he recycles the same water all day.
characters.voice: Adult male, flamboyant showman, bright and projecting, quick dramatic pace.

lines.first_meet: [grandly] Sir Fountain, star of the roundabout! My secret? Same water, round and round. A pump does the jumping.
lines.again: [delighted] My audience returns! Same water, same jets, brand-new sparkle. Showbiz is all lighting, darling.
lines.goodbye: [whispers] Don't drink from me; I've been recycling all week. Somewhere up north, a real waterfall is showing off. Go!

characters.name: Mangrove Mo
characters.personality: A hushed, secretive nursery-keeper of the river delta who runs a kindergarten for fish and prawns. Speaks softly so as not to wake anyone.

lines.first_meet: [hushed] Mangrove Mo, the mangrove creek. Fish and prawns grow up in my roots before going to sea. Shh, they're small.
lines.again: [softly] The tide brought you back? It brings everyone back. Crabs, herons, mud, and now you.
lines.goodbye: [whispers] Stay on the boat or boardwalk; my mud swallows shoes. Look at my roots. They breathe through little pencils!

guardian.name: Old Roundabout
guardian.personality: An old roundabout that has watched every taxi, bus and bicycle circle him for sixty years. Unhurried, fond, a little hoarse from the horns; treats road safety like family.

lines.first_meet: [warm chuckle] Hello! I'm Old Roundabout. Everything with wheels goes round me. Photos from the sidewalk only!
lines.again: [laughs] Back again? You're a regular now, like the school bus. So, who have you brought me today?
lines.goodbye: [softly] Cross at the signal, eyes both ways. The road is full of stories; just don't stand in the middle of one.
lines.hint: [squints] Hmm, can't tell who that is. From the sidewalk, show me the whole vehicle, wheels and all. Or its sign.

characters.name: Sunny
